proposals.before: During the Tang, Prince Ji Ji of Wei served as director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently as military commissioner of Zhenzhou, with the legal officer Li Rao as chief secretary.
proposals.after: During the Tang, Li Jiji, Prince of Wei, served as director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently as military commissioner of Zhenzhou, with the legal officer Li Rao as chief secretary.
proposals.reason: 魏王繼岌 is Li Jiji, Prince of Wei; "Prince Ji Ji of Wei" misorders the title and personal name.

proposals.before: In Tang, Prince Ji Ji of Wei was Director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently held the post of military commissioner of Zhen Prefecture; the legal officer Li Rao was put in charge of secretarial records.
proposals.after: In Tang, Li Jiji, Prince of Wei, was Director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently held the post of military commissioner of Zhen Prefecture; the legal officer Li Rao was put in charge of secretarial records.
proposals.reason: Same name-order repair as idiomatic: 繼岌 is the personal name Jiji under the title Prince of Wei.

proposals.before: Song reached the capital, where Ren Yuan headed the Three Departments and appointed him salt-and-iron commissioner; he later left office and returned home to observe mourning for a parent.
proposals.after: Song reached the capital, where Ren Yuan headed the Three Departments and appointed him salt-and-iron administrative assistant; he later left office and returned home to observe mourning for a parent.
proposals.reason: 鹽鐵判官 is an administrative assistant/judge under the salt-and-iron office, not the commissioner himself.

proposals.before: Song reached the capital; Ren Yuan was director of the Three Departments and employed Song as salt and iron commissioner; he left office and returned to his home district on account of domestic mourning.
proposals.after: Song reached the capital; Ren Yuan was director of the Three Departments and employed Song as salt-and-iron administrative assistant; he left office and returned to his home district on account of domestic mourning.
proposals.reason: 判官 should not be rendered as commissioner.

proposals.before: In the Changxing era, Emperor Mingzong was advanced in years; Prince Qin Li Congrong was often lawless; the Jin high ancestor was deputy commander of the Six Armies, feared calamity would reach him, and sought appointment outside the capital as a frontier commissioner.
proposals.after: In the Changxing era, Emperor Mingzong was advanced in years; Prince Qin Li Congrong was often lawless; Jin Gaozu was deputy commander of the Six Armies, feared calamity would reach him, and sought appointment outside the capital as a frontier commissioner.
proposals.reason: 晉高祖 is the temple name Jin Gaozu (Shi Jingtang), not a literal "high ancestor".

proposals.before: When his parent died he entered mourning, but was recalled to office before the mourning period ended.
proposals.after: When his mother died he entered mourning, but was recalled to office before the mourning period ended.
proposals.reason: 丁內艱 specifically denotes mourning for one's mother, not an unspecified parent.

proposals.before: He entered mourning for a parent and was recalled before mourning was ended.
proposals.after: He entered mourning for his mother and was recalled before mourning was ended.

proposals.before: Later, when the Khitan prince Ma withdrew from Zhenzhou, Song returned with Feng Dao and the others.
proposals.after: Later, when Ma abandoned Zhenzhou, Song returned with Feng Dao and the others.
proposals.reason: Source is 麻棄鎮州; it does not call Ma a Khitan prince in this sentence.

proposals.before: At that time Gaozu was preparing to bury Emperor Ruizong at Ruiling, while Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong.
proposals.after: At that time Gaozu was preparing burial at the Rui Mausoleum, while Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong.
proposals.reason: 睿陵 is a tomb name, not a person Emperor Ruizong.

proposals.before: At that time Gaozu was about to bury Emperor Ruizong at Ruiling; Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong.
proposals.after: At that time Gaozu was about to carry out burial at the Rui Mausoleum; Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong.
proposals.reason: Same 睿陵 misread as a personal title.

proposals.before: When the high ancestor died, the Deposed Emperor took the throne and made Song concurrently administer the Three Departments, sharing command of the Secretariat with Feng Yu.
proposals.after: When Gaozu died, the Deposed Emperor took the throne and made Song concurrently administer the Three Departments, sharing command of the Secretariat with Feng Yu.
proposals.reason: 高祖 is the temple name Gaozu, not 'high ancestor'.

decisions.reason: 魏王 is the title Prince of Wei and 繼岌 is Li Jiji's personal name; the proposed order is correct.
The literal field repeats the same title-name inversion and should identify Li Jiji clearly.
鹽鐵判官 is a subordinate administrative judge or assistant, not the salt-and-iron commissioner.
The literal translation must likewise distinguish 判官 from the commissioner who headed the office.
晉高祖 is the conventional temple name Jin Gaozu, not a phrase meaning 'the Jin high ancestor.'
丁內艱 specifically means entering mourning for one's mother.
The literal field should preserve the explicit maternal mourning indicated by 內艱.

decisions.after: Later, when the Khitan general Mada abandoned Zhenzhou, Song returned with Feng Dao and the others.
decisions.reason: The chapter's 麻 is a truncated reference to the Khitan general Mada (麻荅), identified in parallel passages. Removing the invented princely title is right, but the full attested name should be restored.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 兀欲留其將麻荅守鎮州

decisions.after: At that time Gaozu was about to be buried at Ruiling, while Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong.
decisions.reason: 睿陵 is Gaozu's mausoleum, not an emperor named Ruizong; the construction says Gaozu was about to be interred there.

decisions.after: At that time Gaozu was about to be interred at Ruiling; Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong.
decisions.reason: The literal field must also treat 高祖 as the person being interred and 睿陵 as the mausoleum.
高祖 is a temple name and should remain Gaozu rather than being translated literally as 'high ancestor.'

claimRevisions.reason: The abbreviated or damaged source name is restored from the parallel biography as the Khitan general Mada (麻荅).
